To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a covariatebased stochastic parameterization of the baroclinically unstable ocean circulation can be designed and tested in a way that is both efficient and accurate.

1) a non-Gaussian stochastic approach is necessary for a realistic representation of oceanic eddies; 2) the stochastic parameterization is more accurate when the covariate is flow-dependent; and 3) the stochastic parameterizations are more accurate when the eddy forcing depends on the flow state at the same time as the eddy forcing
the proposed stochastic approach is able to accurately emulate the baroclynic eddy forcing and to capture the corresponding turbulent dynamics of a baroclinic wind-driven ocean circulation.
